cards.text: For seven months the ark of the LORD has been sitting in the land of the Philistines, and city after city has felt the LORD's heavy hand. Now the Philistines call in their priests and diviners and ask them what to do with the ark and how to send it back to its place. SEVEN MONTHS, friend, and I'd have had that thing out the door before my first oven timer went off.

cards.question: True or false: The priests and diviners tell the Philistines they can send the ark of the LORD back empty, with nothing along with it.
The priests and diviners say the ark can't go back to the God of Israel empty. What should go with it?

cards.text: And they add a promise: “Then you will be healed, and you will understand why His hand has not been lifted from you.”

So what goes in the guilt offering? Gold images of the tumors that struck them and of the rats ravaging the land, and friend, I've packed a LOT of apology cookie boxes but never ONE with a gold rat in it.

cards.question: The count of gold tumors and gold rats matches the number of rulers of the Philistines. How many of each do they send?
Along with the gold, what do the priests and diviners tell the Philistines to give the God of Israel?

cards.text: Then the priests and diviners reach back to an old story. They ask the Philistines why they would harden their hearts the way the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened theirs.

cards.question: True or false: The priests and diviners point out that when God afflicted Egypt, the Egyptians sent the people out so they could go on their way.

cards.text: Now comes the plan. One new cart, and two milk cows that have never been yoked.

cards.question: The two milk cows get hitched to the new cart. What happens to their calves?

answers.text: They're taken away and penned up
They walk along beside the cart
They're sent ahead down the road

cards.text: The ark goes on the cart, with a chest of the gold objects right beside it. Then the Philistines send it off, but they keep watching to see if it goes up the road to its homeland, toward Beth-shemesh.

cards.question: If the cart heads up the road toward Beth-shemesh, what will the Philistines know?

answers.text: It was the LORD who brought the disaster
Their own gods have forgiven them
Their offering has been fully accepted

cards.question: True or false: If the cart doesn't head toward Beth-shemesh, the Philistines will decide the disaster happened by chance.

cards.text: So the men do everything as instructed. Cows hitched, calves penned, and the ark loaded on the cart with the chest of gold rats and tumor images.

cards.question: Two milk cows, their calves penned up back home, and an open road. Where do the cows go?

answers.text: Straight up the road toward Beth-shemesh
Back home to their penned up calves
Off the road and into the open fields

cards.text: They stay on that one highway, lowing as they go, never straying to the right or to the left. Friend, those two cows have better lane discipline than ANYBODY I've ever seen in rush hour traffic.

cards.question: True or false: The rulers of the Philistines stay home and wait to hear where the cart ends up.

cards.text: Meanwhile, the people of Beth-shemesh are down in the valley harvesting wheat. They look up, and there it is: the ark.

cards.question: How do the people of Beth-shemesh react when they see the ark coming up the road?

cards.text: No driver, no map, and the cart rolls right into the field of Joshua, a man of Beth-shemesh, and stops near a large rock. Meanwhile I've gotten turned around in my OWN bakery, friend.

cards.question: The cart has stopped in the field near the large rock. What do the people of Beth-shemesh do with the cart and the cows?

answers.text: Chop up the cart and offer the cows to the LORD
Keep the cows and send the cart back home
Send the cart and the cows back to Ekron

cards.question: Who takes the ark of the LORD and the chest of gold down off the cart?

cards.text: They set the ark and the chest on the large rock. That day the men of Beth-shemesh offer burnt offerings and make sacrifices to the LORD.

cards.question: True or false: When the five rulers of the Philistines see all this, they go back to Ekron that same day.

cards.text: Then the passage tallies up the gold: one gold tumor for each Philistine city, Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron, and gold rats to match all the cities of the five rulers, villages included. And that large rock the ark sat on stands to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.
But then the day turns. God strikes down seventy men of Beth-shemesh, and the people mourn.

cards.question: Why does God strike down the men of Beth-shemesh?

answers.text: They kept the gold for themselves

cards.text: And the men of Beth-shemesh ask two big questions: “Who can stand in the presence of the LORD, this holy God? To whom should the ark go up from here?”

cards.question: The men of Beth-shemesh send messengers asking another town to come take the ark. Which town?

cards.text: The message is simple: “The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up with you.” So the men of Kiriath-jearim come for the ark of the LORD and carry it to a house on the hill.

cards.question: The men of Kiriath-jearim bring the ark of the LORD to a house on the hill. Whose house is it?
They consecrate Abinadab's son Eleazar to ___ the ark of the LORD.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set it down for today, friend. Trust me, this story still has more pages in it.

findings.problem: The card says city after city has felt the LORD's heavy hand. That fact comes from 1 Samuel 5, but the card cites only 1 Samuel 6:1-2, so the outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The heavy-hand fact from 1 Samuel 5 is a Bible fact outside the passage, and it is stated without its reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: In 1 Samuel 6:8-9, the priests and diviners are only giving instructions. The card tells it as if it already happened: the ark goes on the cart, and the Philistines send it off and keep watching. The men don't actually do it until 6:10-11, which card 15 then tells again.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Telling the instructions as events changes what the text calls them. In 6:8-9 these are the priests' and diviners' instructions, not things the Philistines have done.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "But then the day turns" says the deaths happen on the same day as the sacrifices. 1 Samuel 6:19 gives no time for when God struck down the men.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The question opens with "They consecrate...". "They" points back to cards the baker can no longer see, and the question never says that "they" are the men of Kiriath-jearim.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This last story card is only the line saying the story isn't over. It tells no verse, but it cites 1 Samuel 7:1.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the "story's not over" line, what should its verses field cite? Should it cite the last verse of the passage, or be left empty or null?
